Applied Materials Tools Up for More Chip Demand
Spending cycle by chip makers expected to stay strong into next year
By Dan Gallagher
Nov. 16, 2017 at 5:50 pm ET
Even Applied Materials AMAT -4.29% knows the party can’t last forever. But the
company doesn’t see the bash ending anytime soon.
In its fiscal fourth quarter earnings report Thursday, the maker of semiconductor
manufacturing gear showed revenue jumping 20% year over year to $3.97 billion. That
makes for the company’s sixth straight quarter of double-digit sales growth, helped
by strong prices for memory chips as well as growing demand for display production
equipment. Operating income hit a record of $1.1 billion, up 41% year over year.
Applied Materials gave an early peek into fiscal 2018. CEO Gary Dickerson said the
company is “confident” in delivering “strong double-digit growth” for the year. The
first quarter, ending in January, is expected to see revenue grow about 25% at the
midpoint of the company’s forecast, exceeding the 21% growth expected by analysts.
Chip equipment is a highly cyclical business that depends on a handful of large
customers who tend to curtail their spending quickly when demand shifts. That
dynamic hasn’t gone away, but the largest chip makers are still working to catch up
with soaring demand as well as update their manufacturing lines with the latest
processes. Last month, Samsung Electronics boosted its planned capital expenditures
to more than $26 billion in semiconductor and display for this year. That compares
with about $11.4 billion spent in these areas last year, estimates Wes Twigg of
